sections.h2: Where is the Lawrence County recorder, and what does the office do?
sections.html:
The Lawrence County Recorder works from the Court House at 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, Ironton, OH 45638. The contact page lists phone 740-533-4314, fax 740-533-4411, an email address at lawrencecountyohiorecorder.org and hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Ironton is both the county seat and the largest city in the county.

The office keeps the permanent record of land transfers. Its common documents page lists warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds, sheriff's deeds, certificates of transfer, affidavits of transfer, life estate terminations and transfer on death designation and confirmation affidavits, along with mortgages and releases, land contracts, plats, powers of attorney, and a long list of liens from mechanic's liens to child support liens.

sections.h2: What does the Lawrence County recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A notice on the recorder's site says the fee for most documents rose by $5.00 on January 1, 2025, when Senate Bill 94 allowed a document preservation surcharge. The new figure is $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. The same notice says half of the recording fees collected go to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, which tracks section 317.32.

sections.h2: How do you avoid the $20 standardization charge in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
Documents prepared after June 30, 2009 must follow the format in section 317.114, and the recorder's guideline page says a nonconforming document draws an additional $20.00. The requirements it lists:

  • A computer font of at least 10 point.
  • Paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 and no larger than 8.5 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink only and no highlighting.
  • One inch margins on each side and the bottom.
  • A 3 inch margin at the top of page one, kept for the recorder, auditor and engineer only, and 1.5 inches at the top of later pages.

The rule leaves out court and taxing authority documents, plats, DD214 discharge papers, state or federal documents and anything executed before the law took effect. The office also offers a margin guidelines PDF for drafters.

sections.h2: What happens at the Lawrence County auditor before the deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
The auditor sits in the same Court House complex at 111 S Fourth Street, with a phone line at (740) 533-4310 and hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. The conveyance step follows section 319.202: the buyer files a statement of value, the seller pays the conveyance fee, and the auditor endorses the deed.

The statutory base is a charge of $1 or ten cents per $100 of value, whichever is greater, in section 319.54(G)(3), and a county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Because a county's combined rate is its own decision, use the Conveyance Fee Calculator on the auditor's website, which the page describes as including the parcel transfer fee. Enter the parcel count and the sale price and it returns the charge.

sections.h2: Which records can you search at the Lawrence County recorder?
sections.html:
The home page lays out what is searchable. The current index covers deeds from 1982 to the present, mortgages from 1988, financing statements from 1989 and leases, liens and miscellaneous records from 1981. An older online index reaches back much further: deed grantor and grantee entries from 1818 to 1984, mortgages from 1834 to 1988, plats from 1818 to 2010 and leases from 1864 to 1981.

  • Index books online include deed volumes 1 through 475 and mortgage volumes 82 through 441.
  • Specialty records include veterans grave plats, mechanical liens and a soldiers discharge index from 1864 to 1865.
  • Staff can help during normal business hours if a search does not return what you expect.

A title search that stops at 1982 can miss older easements or liens, so ask the recorder where the older books begin for your parcel.

sections.h2: What is Lawrence County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Lawrence County is the southernmost county in Ohio and part of Appalachian Ohio, with part of Wayne National Forest inside it. The earliest settlers named in county histories arrived at Hanging Rock along the Ohio River in 1796. It borders Cabell and Wayne Counties in West Virginia and Boyd and Greenup Counties in Kentucky, and it belongs to the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area. The county was formed on December 20, 1816, from parts of Gallia and Scioto Counties, and the seat moved from Burlington to Ironton in 1851. The present courthouse dates to 1908.

Census QuickFacts shows 55,710 residents for July 2025, down 4.3 percent from the April 2020 base, and 26,564 housing units. Owners occupy 72.3 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $144,000 for 2020 to 2024, with median gross rent of $848. Median household income is $58,325 and 15.0 percent of residents live in poverty. The county reported 23 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How did House Bill 186 change second half 2025 tax bills in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
The auditor's home page explains an Inflation Cap Credit on second half 2025 real estate tax bills, which were mailed on July 9, 2026. It is based on new revenue each school district gained from the 20 mill floor compared with the rate of inflation, and it did not change any appraised value. A buyer or title agent reviewing a parcel can see the credit on the auditor's site by searching the parcel.

The auditor printed these credits per $100,000 of residential and agricultural market value, by school district:

  • Chesapeake $20.63, Dawson Bryant $43.61 and Fairland $19.03.
  • Ironton $41.60, Oak Hill $0.00 and Rock Hill $60.10.
  • South Point $16.84, Symmes Valley $30.83 and Lawrence JVS $3.97.

Anyone who paid before the credit was applied needs to take no action, because the overpayment carries forward to the 2026 first half bill. Ask the Lawrence County Auditor how that carried credit should appear on a closing statement.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Lawrence County, Ohio?
faqs.a: Record it with the Lawrence County Recorder at the Court House, 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, Ironton, OH 45638. The phone number is 740-533-4314. The deed visits the county auditor first for the statement of value and conveyance fee.

faqs.q: How much does Lawrence County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The recorder's fee notice shows $39.00 for one or two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, effective January 1, 2025. Reference fees of $4.00 and the $20.00 standardization charge still apply where they are triggered.

faqs.q: Is there a way to estimate the Lawrence County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor's website has a Conveyance Fee Calculator that includes the parcel transfer fee. You enter a parcel count and a sale price and it computes the charge. Ask the auditor's office at (740) 533-4310 if the result looks different from what your closing agent quotes.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed does not meet the Ohio margin rules?
faqs.a: The recorder takes it but collects an additional $20.00. The 3 inch top margin on the first page is kept for the recorder, auditor and engineer. Court papers, plats, DD214s, state or federal documents and older instruments are excluded.

faqs.q: How far back do Lawrence County deed records go online?
faqs.a: The current index lists deeds from 1982 to the present, and the older online index lists deed grantor and grantee entries from 1818 to 1984. Index books run from deed volume 1 through 475. For anything earlier than the index covers, contact the recorder.
